DAMGHANI:v1p293/r15.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p293/r15.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p293/r15.claim: Ṭughyān can mean disobedience; the work applies the same sense to Pharaoh and another prohibition.
DAMGHANI:v1p293/r15.anchor: الطغيان العصيان قوله سبحانه في سورة طه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p22/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p22/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p22/r7.claim: After teaching monotheism and the Hereafter and equipping Moses with miracles, God sends him to warn Pharaoh of his tyranny.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p22/r7.anchor: to try to make him fear God and His wrath

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p23/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p23/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p23/r4.claim: Going to Pharaoh was Moses’ first assigned campaign; Pharaoh claimed divinity and was treated as the Egyptians’ sun deity’s avatar.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p23/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p23/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p23/r5.claim: Pharaoh’s oppression included killing or drowning Israelite boys and keeping girls alive as slave-maidens; Moses knew his rebellion from personal suffering.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p23/r5.anchor: put to death or cast into the sea.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p23/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p23/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p23/r6.claim: God leaves Pharaoh’s rebellion unexplained because Moses already knew it and had suffered under it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p23/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p23/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p23/r7.claim: God’s messengers first address society’s leaders because they administer society and their reform can quickly reform the whole community.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p23/r7.anchor: warn the leaders and chiefs of their society.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p24/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p24/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p24/r1.claim: When leaders deny, their hollow reasoning becomes clear; any later acceptance is informed and can persuade others, unlike emotion-driven public campaigns.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p24/r1.anchor: the hollow nature of their logic becomes evident to their followers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p24/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p24/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p24/r2.claim: Movements relying on public emotional propaganda depend on emotion and lack a role for reason.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p24/r2.anchor: Sense and reason have no role in them and neither can they ever have.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p325/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p325/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p325/r7.claim: After showing the miracles, God sends Moses to Pharaoh because he transgressed; Pharaoh is singled out as the head of disbelief and claimant to divinity, with his people as followers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p325/r7.anchor: أمره بالذهاب إلى فرعون رسولا من عنده تعالى

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r10.claim: Although Pharaoh had greatly transgressed, the command to address him gently shows how important method and tone are to successful religious preaching.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r10.anchor: 24 ve 43. âyetlerde Firavun’a uyarıcı gönderilme gerekçesi olarak “onun sınırı çok aştığı” ifade edildiği halde 44. âyette “Yine de ona söyleyeceklerinizi yumuşak bir üslûpla söyleyiniz

STUDYQURAN:20:24/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:24/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:24/r1.claim: This command is identical to 79:17, parallels the wording in 20:43, and is linked to other Moses narratives.
STUDYQURAN:20:24/r1.anchor: This verse is identical to 79:17 (cf. v. 43); see also 26:10–11; 27:12; 28:32

TABATABAI:20:23-25/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:23-25/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:23-25/r2.claim: The order to go to Pharaoh initiates Moses' mission; the preceding staff and hand signs prepare for it.
TABATABAI:20:23-25/r2.anchor: هذا هو أمر الرسالة وكانت الآيات السابقة

TABRISI:20:17-36/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:17-36/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:17-36/r11.claim: طغيان is exceeding the limit in disobedience.

TABRISI:20:21-28/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:21-28/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:21-28/r15.claim: After entrusting Moses with the mission and showing him the miracles, God commands him to call Pharaoh, who had become arrogant and tyrannical in disbelief.

THALABI:v6p243/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p243/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p243/r1.claim: Pharaoh has disobeyed, exalted himself, grown arrogant, and disbelieved; Moses is told to call him to God's worship.
THALABI:v6p243/r1.anchor: اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى عصى وعلا وتكبر وكفر، فادعه إلى عبادتي

THALABI:v6p243/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p243/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p243/r2.claim: The account says Moses asks how he can approach Pharaoh if God has bound his heart; an angel who keeps the winds urges him to obey God's command.
THALABI:v6p243/r2.anchor: قال: فكيف تأمرني أن آتيه وقد ربطت على قلبه؟ فأتاه ملك من خزان الريح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p387/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p387/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p387/r1.claim: Pharaoh exceeded the bounds of disobedience, committing an extreme transgression beyond that of other people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p387/r1.anchor: {اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى} أي: جاوز القدر في العصيان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p387/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p387/r2.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p387/r2.claim: The People of Meanings supply an ellipsis: Moses was to go to Pharaoh and call him to affirm God’s oneness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p387/r2.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: (وفي الآية محذوف؛ لأن المعنى: إذهب إلى فرعون فادعه إلى توحيد الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:21-26/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:21-26/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:21-26/r6.claim: Pharaoh disbelieved God's blessings and grew arrogant toward His worship.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257/r7.claim: Pharaoh's transgression means that he disbelieved.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257/r7.anchor: {اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى} [طه: 24] يعني: إنه كفر.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257/r8.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257/r8.claim: Al-Suddī explains it as disobeying God; Yahya says this amounts to the same thing.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p257/r8.anchor: وقال السدي: إنه عصى الله. وهو واحد.

QASHANI:20:24/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:24/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:24/r1.claim: Pharaoh signifies the soul's self-assertion, which veils itself and transgresses the limit of servitude.
QASHANI:20:24/r1.anchor: بظهور الأنائية، فاحتجب بها فتعدى عن حد العبودية

QASHANI:20:24/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:24/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:24/r2.claim: Moses' mission occurred at disclosure of the attributes, before his forty-day retreat and essential disclosure after Pharaoh's destruction; thus messengership does not require prior annihilation of the Essence.
QASHANI:20:24/r2.anchor: وهذه الرسالة والدعوة إنما كانت في مقام تجلي الصفات

QASHANI:20:24/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:24/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:24/r3.claim: As further support, most of the Prophet's spiritual journey took place after prophethood, revelation, and guidance through scripture.
QASHANI:20:24/r3.anchor: إن أكثر سير النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بعد النبوة والوحي والاهتداء بالتنزيل

QUSHAYRI:v2p258/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p258/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p258/r3.claim: After honoring Moses with direct speech, God sent him to call Pharaoh despite knowing Pharaoh would not believe or respond; Moses accepted the ordeal over his own wish.
QUSHAYRI:v2p258/r3.anchor: فشق على موسى ذهابه إلى فرعون ، وسماع جحده منه ، بعد ما سمع من الله كلامه سبحانه

NAHHAS:v3p36/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p36/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p36/r9.claim: Pharaoh's طغى means he exceeded the bounds in disbelief.

ASAD-NOTES:20:24#n16/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:24#n16/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:24#n16/r1.claim: Asad identifies Pharaoh's claim to divine status as his greatest sin.
ASAD-NOTES:20:24#n16/r1.anchor: Pharaoh's greatest sin, namely, his claim to divine status

ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r1.claim: The command shifts from preliminary instructions to the passage's central mission; its separation marks the mission's importance.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r1.anchor: تخلص إلى ما هو المقصد من تمهيد المقدمات السالفة فصل عما قبله من الأوامر ايذانا باصالته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r2.claim: Moses is to approach Pharaoh with the great signs, call him to worship God, and warn him of divine punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r2.anchor: أي اذهب اليه بما رايته من آياتنا الكبرى وادعه إلى عبادتى وحذره نقمتى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r3.claim: Pharaoh's transgression explains the command or its obligation: he exceeded bounds in pride and tyranny, daring to claim divinity.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r3.anchor: تعليل للأمر أو لوجوب المامور به أي جاوز الحد في التكبر والعتو والتجبر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r4.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r4.claim: Wahb recounts God steadying Moses, reassuring him of divine sight, hearing, support, and strength, then commissioning him to Pharaoh, whom the report portrays as arrogant and a denier of God's lordship.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r4.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه : أن الله تعالى قال لموسى عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r5.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r5.claim: In Wahb's report, God says Pharaoh could be destroyed but is restrained by the proof and excuse established for creation; Pharaoh is small in God's sight and encompassed by divine forbearance.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r5.anchor: لو لا العذر والحجة اللذان وضعت بينى وبين خلقى لبطشت به بطشة جبار

ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r6.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r6.claim: Wahb's report instructs Moses to convey the message, call Pharaoh to worship and exclusive devotion, warn him, and speak gently, assuring that God hastens to pardon more than to punish.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r6.anchor: فبلغه رسالتى وادعه إلى عبادتى وتوحيدى واخلاص اسمى وذكره بايامى وحذره نقمتى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r7.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r7.claim: Wahb's report says Pharaoh had four hundred years of respite while opposing God, yet received rain, crops, health, youth, wealth, and power through divine patience.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181/r7.anchor: وانه قد امهلك اربعمائة سنة في كلها انت مبارزه بالمحاربة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#2/r1.claim: An unspecified report says Moses remained silent for seven days or longer after being ordered to go; an angel then told him to carry out his Lord's command, and al-Alusi doubts the report.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p181#2/r1.anchor: وفي بعض الروايات أن الله تعالى لما امره عليه السلام بالذهاب إلى فرعون سكت سبعة ايام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270#2/r9.claim: Pharaoh exceeded the bounds in disobedience and rebellion, so Moses is to call him to worship God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p270#2/r9.anchor: {اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى} أي: جاوز الحد في العصيان والتمرد، فادعه إلى عبادتي.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:24/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:24/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:24/r1.claim: Moses is to go to Pharaoh with the two signs and call him to worship.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:24/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:24/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:24/r2.claim: Pharaoh had rebelled and acted arrogantly.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r18.claim: Moses is sent to turn Pharaoh back from rebellion; Pharaoh exceeded the bounds of servanthood and claimed divinity.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r18.anchor: { اذهب إلى فرعون } أي لترده عن عتوه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p16/r19.claim: The statement of Pharaoh’s transgression is emphatic because anyone’s rebellion against the Supreme King is extraordinary.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p42/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p42/r10.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p42/r10.claim: One account names Pharaoh as Musʿab ibn al-Rayyan; Ibn Atiyya says this and the other identifications are unsupported.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p42/r10.anchor: وهو مصعب بن الريان في بعض ما قيل، وقيل غير هذا، ولا صحة لشيء من ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p42/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p42/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p42/r11.claim: طغى means to exceed the limit in corruption.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p42/r11.anchor: وطغى معناه تجاوز الحد في فساد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p281/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p281/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p281/r1.claim: Pharaoh “transgressed” by exceeding the bounds in disobedience.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p281/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى إنه طغى أي جاوز الحد في العصيان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p280#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p280#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p280#2/r1.claim: God sends Moses to Pharaoh, Egypt's king from whom he fled, to call him to worship God alone and treat the Israelites well; Pharaoh transgressed, preferred worldly life, and forgot God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p280#2/r1.anchor: أي: اذهب إلى فرعون ملك مصر، الذي خرجت فارا منه وهاربا، فادعه إلى عبادة الله وحده لا شريك له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p280#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p280#2/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p280#2/r2.claim: Wahb's divine address assures Moses of God's protection, portrays Pharaoh as arrogant despite long respite and abundant provision, orders a gentle summons to monotheism and warning, forbids fear or envy of worldly display, and promises lasting honor for God's friends.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p280#2/r2.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه: قال الله لموسى: انطلق برسالتي فإنك بعيني وسمعي

JISHUMI:v6p4646/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r10.claim: Ṭughyān is exceeding bounds in disobedience; baghy is a parallel term, and ṭughāt and bughāt are paired forms.
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r10.anchor: والطغيان: مجاوزة الحد في العصيان، طغى طغيانا، ونظيره: البغي، ومنه: قوم طغاة بغاة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p62/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p62/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p62/r1.claim: Moses recognized that facing Pharaoh the tyrant was a grave assignment requiring steadfastness and a broad, patient heart; he asked God to expand his chest and ease his task amid great affairs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p62/r1.anchor: عرف أنه كلف أمرا عظيما وخطبا جسيما يحتاج معه إلى احتمال ما لا يحتمله إلا ذو جأش رابط

MUQATIL:20:24-29/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:24-29/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:24-29/r1.claim: Pharaoh has disobeyed; Moses is to call him to worship God, though God has bound Pharaoh's heart so that he will not believe.
MUQATIL:20:24-29/r1.anchor: يقول: إنه عصى، فادعوه إلى عبادتي

MUQATIL:20:24-29/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:24-29/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:24-29/r2.claim: A keeper angel from the storehouses of the wind came to Moses and told him to go and carry out the command.
MUQATIL:20:24-29/r2.anchor: فأتاه ملك خازن من خزان الريح

NASAFI-FULL:v3p53#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53#4/r1.claim: Pharaoh crossed the bounds of servanthood by claiming divinity.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53#4/r1.anchor: جاوز حد العبودية إلى دعوى الربوبية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p53#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53#4/r2.claim: Moses knew this grave assignment required an expanded heart; the commentary begins to introduce that need.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p53#4/r2.anchor: ولما أمره بالذهاب إلى فرعون الطاغي وعرف أنه كلف أمرا عظيما يحتاج إلى صدر فسيح

QURTUBI-FULL:20:24-30/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:24-30/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:24-30/r1.claim: After the staff and hand signs showed Moses was a messenger, he was ordered to summon Pharaoh.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:24-30/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { اذهب إلى فرعون إنه طغى } لما آنسه بالعصا واليد، وأراه ما يدل على أنه رسول،

QURTUBI-FULL:20:24-30/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:24-30/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:24-30/r2.claim: Ṭaghā means disobeyed, became arrogant and disbelieving, tyrannized, and exceeded the limit.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:24-30/r2.anchor: «طغى» معناه عصى وتكبر وكفر وتجبر وجاوز الحد.

BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r1.claim: Moses is to go to Pharaoh and his chiefs by way of preaching and warning, carrying the staff and the hand as his two signs.
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r1.anchor: اذهب} يا موسى بطريق الدعوة والتحذير {إلى فرعون} وملئه بهاتين الآيتين

BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r2.claim: The two proofs are identified as Moses' staff and hand; Bursevī cites the explicit description in al-Qaṣaṣ.
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r2.anchor: لقوله تعالى في سورة القصص {فذانك برهانان من ربك إلى فرعون وملايه}

BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r4.claim: Pharaoh exceeded the bounds of servitude by claiming divinity independently, not as a partner, as in his claim “I am your highest lord.”
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r4.anchor: أي : جاوز حد العبودية بدعوى الربوبية استقلالا لا اشتراكا

BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r5.claim: When a sincere wayfarer reaches completion, God appoints him to guide and train other servants.
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r5.anchor: أن السالك الصادق إذا بلغ مرتبة كماله يقيضه الله لدلالة عباده وتربيتهم

BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r6.claim: The mature return to mix with people and endure their harm, thereby testing their forbearance and forgiveness.
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r6.anchor: أن كمال البالغين في أن يرجعوا إلى الخلق ومخالطتهم والصبر على أذاهم

BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r7.claim: The staff was appropriate because it is a shepherd's tool and Moses had been a shepherd.
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r7.anchor: لأن العصا من آلات الرعاة وموسى عليه السلام كان راعيا

BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p290#2/r8.claim: Bursevī crudely likens Pharaoh to a donkey that required a staff and beating; Rūmī's cited verses elaborate this image of correction and warning.

RAZI-FULL:v22p27/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p27/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p27/r1.claim: After showing Moses the sign, God sends him to Pharaoh because Pharaoh transgressed; although Moses was sent to all, Pharaoh is singled out for claiming divinity, arrogance, and being a leader followed by others.
RAZI-FULL:v22p27/r1.anchor: لما أظهر له هذه الآية عقبها بأن أمره بالذهاب إلى فرعون وبين العلة في ذلك وهي أنه طغى

RAZI-FULL:v22p27/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p27/r2.speaker: وهب
RAZI-FULL:v22p27/r2.claim: Wahb reports God’s charge to Moses: deliver the message, summon Pharaoh to worship, warn him, speak gently, and trust God’s protection and knowledge over the arrogant ruler; no grading is given.
RAZI-FULL:v22p27/r2.anchor: قال وهب : قال الله تعالى لموسى عليه السلام : ( اسمع كلامي واحفظ وصيتي وانطلق برسالتي

RAZI-FULL:v22p27/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p27/r3.speaker: وهب
RAZI-FULL:v22p27/r3.claim: Wahb adds that Moses remained silent for seven days, after which an angel came and told him to answer his Lord’s command to go to Pharaoh.
RAZI-FULL:v22p27/r3.anchor: قال فسكت موسى سبعة أيام لا يتكلم ثم جاءه ملك فقال أجب ربك فيما أمرك بعبده
